x: Youngest of these was Ian Gillings who was only eight years old at the time and yet managed to place 27th - a tremendous little runner! The College gave us a fine tea afterwards and we were waited upon by some of the older boys.

The Boys 880 yds produced a good winner and the most popular competitor of the afternoon---8½yrs old Ian Gillings. Half the size and only two-thirds the age of many of his rivals he was by no means outclassed.
NOT FAIR that 'Little' Ian Gillings trains with the big boys - their pride wont let them 'drop' and Little Ian duffed up our aimiable giant Bob Glover round the Park (Battersea) the other day.

I expect he has heard of the new training methods being tried out at Battersea, and wishes to include them in some book or other he is writing. Ian Gillings was not interested in running against him, he say he is saving himself for a go at Jim Ryun!
Nine-year-old Ian Gillings, not content with a stylish run in the 'half', went pot hunting in the interval and scooped a prize in the children's race; after a flyer too!
L.to R: John Crockford, Mick Harvey(12), Ian Gillings(9), Vic Butcher(10), Richard Langley(7),Michael Kane(3),Bill Keohane(rear),Martin Bloice(6) Reg Hopkins(2), Eddie McNally.

…hand him the bronze medal, although the record will still place him third - a very nice gesture and most sportsmanlike. Ian Gillings was a worthy winner of the handicap - still only 11 years old he is running like a veteran!…
Ian Gillings (all 3ft 6in of him) talking like old pals to David Hemery (all 6ft of him). What a true champion, always ready to give time even in the middle of a meeting to youngsters.
Ian Gillings was leading the field with only a quarter of a mile to go but was forced to drop out with stitch. Never mind Ian, it happens to the best of them.
Ian Gillings won the Kingston district (1st year) boys C.C. Championships and went on through to the Surrey Schools on Febuary 7th.

Ken looks a promising lad and could well follow in the footsteps of our present band of successful youngsters. Young Reg Hopkins was a good third, while Ian Gillings with several years ahead in the Boys ranks showed improved form.
Our very young team of Colts did excellently, gaining third team medals, Ian Gillings being placed second in 14m. 54s., some 32s. behind the winner, A.

Crosbie fourth in the javelin, while Ian Gillings can look forward next year to showing a sharp improvement on this year's sixth place in his 1,500m. heat, a performance which does not reflect his full talent.
It was only the experience of Ian Gillings (it seems incredible with one so young, but Ian has been running for four years now) that brought him success from Andrew Martell.

The day before the race our team, Bob Glover and Charlie Manning, flushed with success from their recent 5,000 metre Club Championship, were out from their training camp and did two laps of the course with Ted Stimpson, Ian and Martin Gillings.
Nice to see Ian and Martin Gillings in action again, we hear they have been doing some great running at school. If we were to give a medal for perseverance it would have to go to Ivan Beaumont.
